internal.title: Incident Report: Kafka Consumer Lag Impacting Accounting Service
internal.body:
At 10:33 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for high Kafka consumer lag in the accounting service. The lag reached approximately 5200 records, correlating with increased processing latency (p95 latency of 5.2 seconds) but without increased error rates or resource exhaustion. Multiple attempts to mitigate the issue by scaling or restarting services were blocked due to missing dry run approvals and invalid rollback configurations. The diagnosis confirmed that the Kafka consumer lag was causing processing delays. The incident was escalated for further investigation and resolution.

Timeline:
- 10:33:25 UTC: Alert received for KafkaConsumerLagHigh.
- 10:53:06 UTC: Initial diagnosis identified Kafka consumer lag.
- 10:53:07 UTC: Proposed mitigation actions blocked by guardrails.
- 10:53:12 UTC: Confirmed Kafka consumer lag causing processing delay.
- 10:53:13 UTC: Further mitigation proposals blocked.
- 10:53:19 UTC: Additional diagnosis on checkout service errors.

Actions taken were limited due to deployment guardrails preventing scaling or restarts without dry run approvals. The root cause remains unverified due to lack of recovery confirmation. The incident has been escalated for further handling.

external.title: Processing Delays in Accounting Service Due to Kafka Lag
external.body: Between 10:33 and 10:53 UTC on 2026-11-08, customers may have experienced delays in processing within the accounting service. This was caused by a backlog in message processing from Kafka, leading to slower response times. Our team identified the issue promptly and is actively working on a resolution. We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your patience.

output.summary: Kafka consumer lag caused processing delays in the accounting service, leading to increased latency without errors. Mitigation attempts were blocked by deployment guardrails.
output.impact: Customers experienced slower processing times in the accounting service during the incident window, potentially affecting transaction processing speed.
output.root_cause: High Kafka consumer lag causing processing delays in the accounting service was identified as the primary issue. However, recovery was not verified due to blocked mitigation actions.
output.resolution: The incident was escalated for further investigation and resolution due to inability to apply mitigation actions within deployment constraints.
